session_control.side_effects: Changes session access level 0 to 1. Three wrong passwords pulse SALARM for 1 s (S22 p.7.33); factory default OUT101 := HALARM OR SALARM (S22 Table 4.83) closes the alarm contact, and SER4 := SALARM (S22 Table 4.122) records it in the SER. One attempt per session; no further ACC after a failure. Sent only by the transport auth phase. If the Level 1 password is disabled, ACC goes straight to '=>' with no prompt (S22 p.7.33); the adapter sends the password only after seeing 'Password: ?', otherwise the password would be executed as a command and logged (D26, raised by A6).
session_control.notes: Changes session access level only. One attempt per invocation (risk D2).

session_control.side_effects: Returns to Level 0. Without QUIT a Telnet session stays at its elevated level until TIDLE expires (S22 p.7.15-7.16 Telnet Server note).
session_control.notes: Sent twice per session. (1) Once at Level 0 before ACC as the language probe: if rejected, close without elevating and raise the LANG alarm (A1, ADR-0005 4687c17). (2) At the end of every session, followed by a TCP close. No Spanish command starts with QUI. Probe behaviour on a Spanish-mode relay is simulated, not proven.

denied.side_effects: 2AC: SALARM pulses after successful Level 2 access or if access is denied (S22 p.7.33).
denied.notes: Access elevation. Collector holds no Level B/P/A/O/2 password; a failed attempt still counts toward the ALARM pulse (D2).

notes: Revision 2 by A2 (content owner), 2026-10-24, from A1's Phase 0 conversion: C3 review changes 3 and 4 and the sel.ser.other_args citation (docs/phase1/reviews/C3-A2.md). Allowlist decisions are unchanged.

Converted by A1 on 2026-10-24 from the Phase 0 draft (register status: draft; A1 approved SHO G and SHO P 1 on 2026-10-23 (docs/agent-handoffs.md, commit 4481653 on claude/project-thread-hperik); A6 re-review pending; allowlist status: Accepted by A1 for the simulated slice on 2026-10-23 (ADR-0005). The R400-R402 condition is accepted: SHO P 1 must read EHTTP := N, or collection is refused. The inheritance inference is classed 'inferred'. Before collecting from any real relay, the owner must either get SEL to confirm it or accept the inference in writing (owner pre-production list). A6 checks the list independently. UPDATE 2026-10-23 18:48Z: the owner accepted the inheritance inference as an owner risk (ADR-0005). The allowed entries are classed 'inferred (owner-accepted)', never 'documented'.).

Matching (Phase 0): Each pattern is a Python re.fullmatch against one received line. Allowed entries are exact canonical forms the adapter may send. Denied entries document known dangerous lines and are case-insensitive and abbreviation-tolerant on purpose. Any line matching no entry is a violation (deny by default).

Not representable as lines (Phase 0): The password line sent after ACC prompts 'Password:'. It must be logged by the simulator as an auth event, never as a command line, and never stored in clear. | Binary SEL Fast messages (0xA5 prefix, S10). Covered by sel.binary.any_non_ascii below only if the log decodes bytes as latin-1; the checker's CONTROL class misses 0x80-0xFF.

Language (Phase 0): ENGLISH ONLY. Valid only for LANG := ENGLISH on the port. With LANG := SPANISH, command names differ and 'SER D' clears the SER ('SER D o R  Borrar los datos SER', S22 Command Summary); 'SHO' becomes 'MOS' and 'QUIT' becomes 'SAL'. Ruling (A1, ADR-0005 401ebd7, from A6 F-006): the adapter reads LANG with 'SHO P 1' before any SER command and refuses to collect, failing closed with an alarm, unless the output parses as English port settings with LANG := ENGLISH. An 'Invalid Command' or any unparseable response counts as not English. Accepted by A1 (ADR-0005 4687c17): send 'QUI' once at Level 0 before 'ACC'. In English it is valid at Level 0 (S22 Table 7.59). If a Spanish-mode relay rejects it, the adapter learns that before elevating and closes without 'ACC'. This also covers the D18 problem that 'QUI' might not de-elevate a Spanish-mode session. Whether a Spanish-mode relay accepts English names is not documented (unknown). FTPACC or HTTPACC above 1 gets the same warning as MAXACC.

Firmware rule (Phase 0): A1 (ADR-0005 6d82243): collect only from allowlisted FIDs that carry every communications-restart fix. Appendix A records each fix only on the branches where SEL shipped it, and never says whether other branches had the defect. Each branch's first release (V0) has no 'Includes' clause, so inheritance across branches is not documented. Treating a fix as inherited by a branch whose V0 is dated after the fix is an INFERENCE, marked as such. It needs SEL confirmation before it counts as documented.

Firmware match (Phase 0): Match the full FID string: SEL-751-R<branch>-V<n>-Z<...>-D<date>, with V >= min_version on an allowed branch and the Z and D fields equal to an Appendix A row. Any FID not in Appendix A (later releases, special builds, SEL-751A) is unknown and fails closed.
